text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Hariri asks those criticising the government's latest decisions -- which raised custom duties on cars and banned imports of some food items -- to come up with alternative policies.
- Foreign Minister Bouez: The vote calling on Israel to pay for damage resulting from its April 1996 shelling of a U.N. south Lebanon camp in Qana is a victory for Lebanon and the United Nations.
- Fugitive businessman Tamraz detained in Georgia after eight years on the run.
- Palestinian camps in Lebanon strike to protest against the U.S. congressional resolution calling on President Clinton to reaffirm that Jeruslame must remain Isarel's undivided capital.
- More evacuees arrive in Beirut from Africa.
- One Israeli sodier killed and three wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon.
- Malaysian Prime Minister in Beirut today.
- Hariri meets Syrian President Assad and Vice President Khaddam. Coordination between the two countries is most important at this stage.
